title: Coherent marked cone calculations on generators
statement:
Use coherent realization and small simplicial categories of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], marked objects and weak equivalences of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], the marked-anodyne generators of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], and projective diagrams of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. For a small simplicial set $S$, a small simplicial category $I$ and a simplicial functor $u:\mathfrak C[S]\to I^{\mathrm{op}}$, define a marked $I$-diagram $L_u(X)$ for a marked map $X\to S$ as follows. Put $P_X=I^{\mathrm{op}}\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]$, with new cone vertex $v$, and $L_u(X)(i)=P_X(i,v)$. Precomposition gives the $I$-action, with each mapping simplicial set acting with all its edges marked, as for the tensor defining the simplicial model enrichment. The edge $e:x\to y$ gives a cone edge $\widetilde e:\widetilde x\to u(e)^*\widetilde y$; mark the edges $g^*\widetilde e$ for marked $e$ and every $g\in I^{\mathrm{op}}(i,u(x))_1$. Include all degenerate edges. 
For the canonical index $I=\mathfrak C[S]^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $u=\mathrm{id}$, the following generator calculations hold. For $S=\Delta^n$, $L_u((\partial\Delta^n)^\flat)\to L_u((\Delta^n)^\flat)$ is a projective cofibration, including $n=0$. For $S=\Delta^1$, $L_u((\Delta^1)^\flat)\to L_u((\Delta^1)^\sharp)$ is a projective cofibration. For each one of the four types of marked-anodyne generator $j:A\to B$ listed in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], take $S$ to be the underlying simplicial set of $B$. Then $L_{\mathrm{id}}(j)$ is a projective trivial cofibration. No local Kan hypothesis on $\mathfrak C[S]$ is imposed.
For terminal $I$ and $S=\Delta^0$, write $T=L_u$. Let $Q^n$ be the cosimplicial simplicial set of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], with its subset-cube quotient description and its maps $Q^n\to\Delta^n$ induced by $J\mapsto\max J$. The cone pushout for $(\Delta^n)^\flat$ is the coherent realization of $\Delta^{n+1}$ with its initial face $\Delta^n$ collapsed, so the underlying simplicial set of $T((\Delta^n)^\flat)$ is $Q^n$, naturally in $[n]$, and the underlying functor is the coend $T(X)=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}X_n\times Q^n$. The maps $Q^n\to\Delta^n$ induce a natural underlying map $T(X)\to X$, and this map preserves markings. For $(\Delta^0)^\flat$, $(\Delta^1)^\flat$ and $(\Delta^1)^\sharp$ it is an isomorphism of marked simplicial sets.

source.place: Propositions 3.2.1.7 and 3.2.1.11 restricted to their explicit generators; Section 2.2.2, max augmentation (Q^n itself is stated in lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching); calculation used in Proposition 3.2.1.14. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this marked simplicial or infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Form the pushout (P_X=I^{\mathrm{op}}\amalg_{\mathfrak C[X]}\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]). The coherent-realization construction is defined by colimits over simplices, and composition in each coherent simplex is union of subsets, so the pushout has the stated cone vertex (v), cone arrows, and relations. Precomposition by (I^{\mathrm{op}}) gives the (I)-diagram structure. The simplicial tensor in the marked model acts by the sharp marking, hence every edge of an acting mapping simplicial set is marked; applying it to the triangle for (e:x\to y) gives (g^*\widetilde e), and the union composition law sends it to ((hg)^*\widetilde e). Marked edges and all degeneracies are therefore closed under the action. A map of marked (X\to S) carries these generators to the corresponding generators, so (L_u) is functorial. The projective diagram model exists for the small simplicial category (I), with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, and no local-Kan condition on (I) is needed.

source.place: Construction preceding Definition 3.2.1.2 and Definition 3.2.1.2; Proposition 3.2.1.4(1); Appendix A.3.3.

proof.text: For $S=\Delta^n$, write $F_0(W)=I(0,-)\otimes W$ for the free diagram at vertex $0$. Since $I=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]^{\mathrm{op}}$, it is $W$ at $0$ and empty at every other vertex. The full cone evaluated at $k$ is the subset cube $(\Delta^1)^{\{k+1,\ldots,n\}}$. In the minimally marked simplex, a cube edge is marked exactly when the maximum of its two endpoint subsets (including $k$) agrees: it is then an acting mapping edge applied to a degenerate cone edge. For $k>0$, the face omitting $0$ already gives the entire evaluated cube. At $0$, the boundary contributes every coordinate-$0$ face by omission of that vertex and every coordinate-$1$ face by composition through that vertex; their intersections are the corresponding simultaneous coordinate conditions, by union of subsets. Thus its evaluation is exactly the cubical boundary, with the restricted marking. The relative diagram is the pushout of $F_0(\partial C\hookrightarrow C)$ for this marked cube $C$. At $n=0$ this means $F_0(\varnothing\to\Delta^0)$, not an attachment of a new cone object to an already nonempty evaluation. The cube-boundary map is injective, hence a marked cofibration. Evaluation preserves projective trivial fibrations, so its left adjoint $F_0$ preserves cofibrations by adjointing lifting squares. The asserted boundary map is therefore a projective cofibration.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.7, boundary computation expanded using the subset cubes.

proof.text: For any fixed underlying $X\to S$, adding a marking on an edge $e:x\to y$ changes no underlying cone simplicial set. It is exactly a pushout of the free diagram at $u(x)$ applied to $(\Delta^1)^\flat\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, along the map represented by $\widetilde e$. Indeed the free action tensors with the sharp marking on the acting mapping simplicial set, so the new marked edges are precisely all $g^*\widetilde e$ in the definition. Coproducts of these pushouts handle any set of newly marked edges. Each free map is a projective cofibration by the evaluation/free adjunction, since the marked edge inclusion is a cofibration. This proves the canonical marking assertion and also shows that all the pure-marking maps used below are projective cofibrations. Here is the maps-out verification of colimit preservation. Given a marked $I$-diagram $Y$, form a simplicial category $R_Y$ with objects $\operatorname{Ob}(I)\amalg\{v\}$, old mapping objects those of $I^{\mathrm{op}}$, mapping objects $R_Y(i,v)=Y(i)$, $R_Y(v,i)=\varnothing$ and $R_Y(v,v)=\Delta^0$; composition into $v$ is the diagram action. A map $L_u(X)\to Y$ is exactly a simplicial functor $\mathfrak C[X\star\Delta^0]\to R_Y$ extending $u|_{\mathfrak C[X]}$, taking the cone vertex to $v$, and taking each marked elementary cone edge to a marked edge. Naturality forces preservation of all its acting images. For a colimit $X=\operatorname{colim}_a X_a$ over $S$, cone simplices are precisely simplices from the $X_a$ with the cone vertex adjoined, modulo the original identifications and the common cone vertex. Coherent realization preserves these colimits by its simplex-colimit definition. Thus such functors are exactly compatible functors from the original cones; the marking on the colimit is the union of the images of their marking generators. This proves colimit preservation, including the empty colimit, whose cone contributes no maps from old objects to $v$.

source.place: Definition 3.2.1.2 and Proposition 3.2.1.4(1); marking case of Proposition 3.2.1.7.

proof.text: Let $j:(\Lambda_i^n)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$, $0<i<n$, and use $S=\Delta^n$. Every evaluation at $k>0$ is unchanged, since its cone cube uses only vertices $k,\ldots,n$, all lying in a face of the horn. At $0$ put $K=(\Delta^1)^{\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}}$, $K'=\partial K$, and use coordinate $i$ as the last factor of $K\times\Delta^1$. The subset formula gives the relative cube domain $B=(K'\times\Delta^1)\cup(K\times\{1\})$: omitting a vertex different from $i$ gives its coordinate-$0$ face, and composing through a vertex gives its coordinate-$1$ face. The only missing face is coordinate $i=0$. Put $A=\{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}:J\text{ contains some }j>i\}$. The nondegenerate vertical edge over $J$ has unchanged maximum exactly when $J\in A$. All other marked edges of the full cube already lie in $B$: their common maximum gives either a constantly $1$ coordinate of $K$ or the face $i=1$. Consequently the relative marked cube is a pushout of the selectively marked cylinder of [lem-coef-selectively-marked-terminal-cylinder], adding the already present markings on $B$. A nondegenerate simplex of $K$ outside $\partial K$ is a chain of subsets whose union is the full coordinate set; its final vertex therefore contains $n>i$ and lies in $A$. The cylinder lemma applies. The whole relative diagram is the pushout of $F_0$ of this marked-anodyne map. A marked-anodyne map is a marked trivial cofibration: its restriction maps into every fibrant target are trivial Kan fibrations by the lifting-calculus statement, and the marked-model weak-equivalence test applies. The free/evaluation adjunction therefore makes this a projective trivial cofibration.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(1), with Lemma 3.2.1.9; the affected vertex is 0 (the later v_n in the printed proof is a subscript typo).

proof.text: For the final-horn generator with $n>1$, put $K=(\Delta^1)^{\{1,\ldots,n-1\}}$, $K'=\partial K$, use coordinate $n$ as the interval factor, and put $A=\{J:n-1\in J\}$. The noninitial evaluations are unchanged. At $0$ the same subset calculation gives $B=(\partial K\times\Delta^1)\cup(K\times\{1\})$: faces omitting $j<n$ give coordinate $j=0$, composites through $j$ give coordinate $j=1$, and only coordinate $n=0$ is absent. The marked final input edge (marked in source and target alike) contributes, among the vertical edges, precisely those above subsets containing $n-1$; in the source only those lying in $B$ are present. Every other marked edge outside this specified vertical set lies in $B$, since a fixed maximum or a fixed $n-1$ coordinate lies on a cube face. Every simplex of $K$ outside its boundary ends at the full subset, which contains $n-1$. The selectively marked cylinder lemma applies with these data, and the relative diagram is again a pushout of its image under $F_0$, hence a projective trivial cofibration. For $n=1$, the horn is the vertex $1$; its evaluation at $0$ is the endpoint inclusion $\{1\}^\sharp\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, which is exactly the dimension-one final-horn generator. Evaluation at $1$ is the identity. Its free-at-$0$ pushout proves this remaining case without a positive-dimensional-cube assumption.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(2), with explicit changed coordinates and n=1 case.

proof.text: We will use the following consequence of the cited marked-model and composition statements. Suppose $E\subseteq E'$ are markings on the same simplicial set $V$, and every map $h:V\to Z$ to a quasicategory that carries $E$ to equivalences also carries $E'$ to equivalences. Then $V_E\to V_{E'}$ is a marked weak equivalence. Indeed an $r$-simplex of $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(V_E,Z^\natural)$ is a map $H:V\times\Delta^r\to Z$. Each slice at a vertex of $\Delta^r$ carries $E'$ to equivalences by hypothesis. For an edge $(e,\alpha)$ with $e\in E'$, the product has a triangle decomposing it into $(e,\mathrm{id})$ followed by $(\mathrm{id},\alpha)$. The first image is an equivalence by the slice assertion, and the second is an equivalence by the original sharp mapping condition. Their diagonal is an equivalence by composition in $hZ$. Thus $H$ preserves $E'\times(\Delta^r)^\sharp$. The two sharp mapping simplicial sets are equal, and the weak-equivalence test applies. This uses the statement of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], which identifies composition from triangles and equivalences with invertible classes, not any unstated property of its proof.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.1.10; direct proof using the sharp mapping-space criterion.

proof.text: For the third generator the only changed evaluation is at $0$. It has underlying square $(\Delta^1)^2$, whose vertices we call $a=(0,0),b=(1,0),c=(0,1),d=(1,1)$. Here $a,b,c,d$ are the subsets $\varnothing,\{1\},\{2\},\{1,2\}$ of the cube over $\{1,2\}$. The source marks $ab,bd,cd$ and the degenerate edges: $ab=\widetilde{01}$, $bd$ is the vertex $\{0,1\}$ acting on $\widetilde{12}$, and $cd$ is an acting edge of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^2](0,2)$ on the cone vertex $\widetilde 2$ (equal maxima). The target marks in addition $ac=\widetilde{02}$. The diagonal $ad$ is not of the form $g^*\widetilde e$ (it is marked in neither, since markings are not closed under composition); it suffices that the argument below covers it as well. For any map of the square to a quasicategory preserving the source markings, the triangle $abd$ gives $[ad]=[bd][ab]$, hence $ad$ is an equivalence; the triangle $acd$ gives $[ad]=[cd][ac]$, hence $ac$ is an equivalence. These are all the previously unmarked nondegenerate edges, so in particular every edge marked in the target is carried to an equivalence. Step 6 therefore makes this evaluation a marked weak equivalence. All other evaluations are isomorphisms, and step 3 makes the entire pure-marking diagram map a projective cofibration. Objectwise weak equivalences are projective weak equivalences, so this is a projective trivial cofibration. No unsupported claim that objectwise cofibrations are projective cofibrations is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(3); two explicit square triangles replace the final marking-anodyne shortcut.

proof.text: For the fourth generator $K^\flat\to K^\sharp$, the underlying cone diagram is unchanged. Write its markings at a vertex $w$ as $E_w\subseteq E'_w$ on $X_w$. Every added marking is $g^*\widetilde e$ for an edge $e:x\to y$ of $K$ and $g\in\mathfrak C[K](w,x)_1$. For any such $e$, fill the $\Lambda^2_0$ horn with $01=e$ and $02=\mathrm{id}_x$, obtaining $e':y\to x$ and a triangle $(e,e',\mathrm{id}_x)$. Fill the $\Lambda^2_0$ horn with $01=e'$ and $02=\mathrm{id}_y$, obtaining $e'':x\to y$ and a triangle $(e',e'',\mathrm{id}_y)$. These fillings are exactly instances of the definition of Kan complex; $e''=e$ is not assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed pp.175-176; returned step 8 separated into horn witnesses, cone-square calculation, categorical inverse algebra, and parameter-edge comparison.

proof.text: Fix $h:X_x\to Z$ carrying $E_x$ to equivalences. Apply [lem-coef-cone-triangle-mapping-square] to the first triangle. Its consecutive edges at $(0,0)\to(1,0)\to(1,1)$ are $\widetilde e$ and $e^*\widetilde e'$; the other two sides are marked because the long input edge is $\mathrm{id}_x$. The two triangles of the square and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] imply that $ba$ is invertible in $hZ$, where $a=[h(\widetilde e)]$ and $b=[h(e^*\widetilde e')]$. Apply the same square lemma to the second triangle and precompose by the constant vertex $e$. It preserves the minimal markings, so the other two sides remain marked. The two triangle equations now make $cb$ invertible, where $c=[h(e^*(e')^*\widetilde e'')]$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed pp.175-176; returned step 8 separated into horn witnesses, cone-square calculation, categorical inverse algebra, and parameter-edge comparison.

proof.text: Put $q=ba$ and $r=cb$ in the ordinary category $hZ$. Then $R=a q^{-1}$ is a right inverse of $b$ and $L=r^{-1}c$ is a left inverse. The identity $L=L(bR)=(Lb)R=R$ makes $b$ invertible, and $a=b^{-1}q$ is invertible. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], $h(\widetilde e)$ is an equivalence edge. This is only categorical inverse algebra on the two invertible composites already obtained.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed pp.175-176; returned step 8 separated into horn witnesses, cone-square calculation, categorical inverse algebra, and parameter-edge comparison.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $w$, a test map $h:X_w\to Z$ carrying $E_w$ to equivalences, and an edge $e:x\to y$ of $K$. For each vertex $a\in\mathfrak C[K](w,x)_0$, precomposition $a^*:X_x\to X_w$ preserves minimal markings by [lem-coef-cone-triangle-mapping-square]. The preceding argument applied to $h\circ a^*$ makes $h(a^*\widetilde e)$ an equivalence. The precomposition action is a marked map $\mathfrak C[K](w,x)^\sharp\times(X_x,E_x)\to(X_w,E_w)$: acting on a generator $g^*\widetilde d$ gives the generator $(ga)^*\widetilde d$ by associativity, and a degenerate edge of $X_x$ is marked after acting: every vertex of $X_x$ is $c^*\widetilde t$ for a vertex $t$ of $K$ and a vertex $c\in\mathfrak C[K](x,t)_0$, since the only arrows into the cone vertex end with a cone arrow, and the coning edge of the degenerate edge of $t$ is the degenerate edge at $\widetilde t$; so acting by an edge $b$ sends that degenerate edge to the generator $(cb)^*\widetilde{s_0t}$, with $cb\in\mathfrak C[K](w,t)_1$. Apply [lem-coef-marked-action-edge-comparison] with this action and the edge $\widetilde e$. It makes $h(g^*\widetilde e)$ an equivalence for every acting edge $g$, without a Kan hypothesis on $\mathfrak C[K](w,x)$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed pp.175-176; returned step 8 separated into horn witnesses, cone-square calculation, categorical inverse algebra, and parameter-edge comparison.

proof.text: Every added marking belongs to the set tested in the preceding step. Step 6 therefore makes each $(X_w,E_w)\to(X_w,E'_w)$ a marked weak equivalence. Step 3 supplies a projective cofibration for this pure-marking map, and the projective model has objectwise weak equivalences by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Thus the fourth generator maps to a projective trivial cofibration. If $K$ is empty there are no evaluations and this assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1.11(4), printed pp.175-176; returned step 8 separated into horn witnesses, cone-square calculation, categorical inverse algebra, and parameter-edge comparison.

proof.text: For terminal (I) and (S=\Delta^0), write (T=L_u). The cone pushout for ((\Delta^n)^\flat) is (\mathfrak C[J^n](x,y)), so the pinched-cube calculation identifies its underlying simplicial set with (Q^n), including the subset-cube quotient and the maps induced by (J\mapsto\max J). Because coherent realization is a colimit over simplices, these identifications assemble to the coend (T(X)=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}X_n\times Q^n). The maximum maps give a natural map (T(X)\to X); a marked cone generator maps to its original marked edge (or to a degenerate edge), so this map preserves markings. For (X=(\Delta^0)^\flat,(\Delta^1)^\flat,(\Delta^1)^\sharp), the quotient has respectively one vertex, the two endpoint/edge simplices, and the same edge with its marking, hence the augmentation is an isomorphism of marked simplicial sets.
